findings.specText: docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.5: "**Duplicates** (`[USDC, USDC]`): both entries snapshot the same balance. The first transfer drains it; the second either reverts on insufficient balance or transfers into a now-empty pot. Either way it fails closed and harms only the caller. No dedupe pass" — read against §4.2: "The dispatcher donates reward token into this contract on every mint. Reading balances *before* the loop means the batcher is paid only the **prior accumulated pot**; the donations generated by their own batch stay behind to seed the next claimant... it is the only thing preventing a caller from **funding their own reward within a single transaction**."
findings.actualBehavior: Duplicates do NOT fail closed in the configuration §4.2 itself assumes. The snapshot pass records `snapshot[i] = B` for every duplicate entry (B = pre-loop balance). The mint loop then increases the balance by the batch's OWN per-mint donation D (BalancerPoolerV2 at the pinned DISPATCHER_INDEX=4 forwards a `donationSplit`% USDC cut to `batchMinter` on every dispatch; primeToken is USDS, so USDC is a legal reward token and the §4.1 exclusion does not fire). The payout pass then transfers B once per entry against a balance of B+D. With k entries the caller extracts k*B whenever k*B <= B+D — i.e. the caller recaptures up to 100% of their own batch's donations. Empirically proven (workspace PoC, 2/2 passing): with B = 3e6 and D = 15e6, 2 duplicate entries pay the recipient 2*B and leave only D-B behind; 6 duplicate entries drain the contract to zero, paying the batcher `priorPot + all of its own donations`.
findings.deviation: The story's own intent is unsafe, not merely mis-implemented. §4.5's stated justification for omitting a dedupe pass ("fails closed and harms only the caller") is factually false under §4.2's donating-dispatcher premise, and the resulting behaviour is precisely the "self-funded round-trip" that §4.2 declares load-bearing to prevent. The two sections of the same normative document contradict each other, and the implementation faithfully follows the wrong one. Cost to the attacker is zero marginal mints — the duplicate array is free relative to an honest single-entry claim, so this strictly dominates honest behaviour for every claimant, and the standing donate-forward pot degenerates to nothing.
findings.impact: Protocol-funded incentive (SYA 30% USDC drip + BalancerPoolerV2 secondary cut) is recaptured by the batcher that generated it instead of seeding the next claimant. The donate-forward mechanic — the entire point of §4.2 — collapses. No user principal is at risk; this is a value leak of protocol-directed funds and a defeat of a documented invariant.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) cap each payout at the live balance and skip on shortfall, (b) accumulate per-token amounts into a deduped payout map, or (c) re-read `balanceOf` at payout and pay `min(snapshot[i], balance)` while zeroing subsequent duplicate entries. Note (c) must NOT be implemented as a plain re-read — that is the §4.2 trap. Whichever is chosen, §4.5 must be rewritten and `test_DuplicateRewardTokenFailsClosed` must be re-armed with a donating dispatcher (see F-20-02).

findings.specText: docs/multi-token-nudge.md §6: "Documented-behaviour witnesses (these encode §4.4/§4.5 so a future change that 'fixes' them fails loudly and forces a docs update) ... 20. `test_DuplicateRewardTokenFailsClosed`."
findings.actualBehavior: The witness calls `_fundPots()` only and never configures `nftMinter.setPerMintDonations(...)`. It therefore exercises the single configuration (D == 0) in which the §4.5 claim happens to hold, and passes green while the property it is supposed to encode is false in the production configuration (see F-20-01). The sibling §4.2 witnesses (`test_OwnDonationsDoNotRefundToBatcher`, `test_SecondBatcherReceivesFirstBatchersDonations`) DO configure donations, so the omission is inconsistent within the same file.
findings.deviation: The §6 witness does not witness the documented behaviour it names; it provides false assurance for §4.5.

findings.specText: story-021 commit f65aec9 body: "`depositFor` settles existing pending via `_safePayTo(user, ...)` rather than `_safePay(...)`, which would pay the migrator." And the ported NatSpec in src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:865-872: "DELTA vs `NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor`: ... `msg.sender` here is the MIGRATOR, so the `_safePay` form would route an existing staker's earned phUSD to the orchestrator while emitting `Claimed(user, ...)`. Only reachable when the deposit target already holds a position ... but wrong in every case."
findings.specSource: git commit f65aec9 body + src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol NatSpec
findings.actualBehavior: `NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor` still calls `pending = _safePay(pending);` at line 756, and `_safePay` delegates to `_safePayTo(msg.sender, ...)` (line 593-595). Under `onlyMigrator`, `msg.sender` is the migrator contract, so an existing staker's settled phUSD is transferred to the orchestrator while `Claimed(user, pending)` is emitted at line 757 naming the user. The staker's `committedDebt` is decremented as though the user was paid. Reachable via `InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.migrateIn` (src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:226) or `NFTStakerMigrator.migrate` (src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:102) whenever the deposit target already holds a non-zero position — e.g. a parked user who re-staked directly between `finalizeAndReset` and `migrateIn`, or a user migrating into a staker they are already in. Recovery: `InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.rescueERC20` (line 268) is an unconditional owner sweep so the funds are recoverable there; `NFTStakerMigrator` has NO rescue function at all (its only externals are `initiateMigration` and `migrate`), so phUSD routed to it is permanently stranded.
findings.deviation: story-021 identifies this exact defect in its own commit message and NatSpec, calls it "wrong in every case", and then explicitly declares `NFTStakerDepletion.sol` untouched (verified: `git show --stat f65aec9` lists only 3 NEW files). The fix landed in the new fourth copy only. The original — the contract that is actually paired with the two live migrators — retains the bug.
findings.impact: Misdirected user reward (value loss, unrecoverable on the `NFTStakerMigrator` path) plus a false `Claimed` event that misleads indexers and any off-chain reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the one-line fix into `src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol:756` (`_safePayTo(user, pending)`). Report as a security finding, not a spec note — it is a live misdirection of user funds in an in-scope contract.

findings.specText: story-021 commit f65aec9 body: "Side-by-side fourth copy of the staker"; src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:36-40: "MAINTENANCE COUPLING: this is a HAND-MAINTAINED copy of `NFTStakerPriceScaled` (which is itself a hand-maintained copy of `NFTStaker`). Any future fix or audit change to either is NOT automatically inherited here and MUST be mirrored manually."
findings.specSource: git commit f65aec9 body + contract NatSpec
findings.actualBehavior: The repo now carries four hand-maintained ~1000-line stakers (NFTStaker, NFTStakerPriceScaled, NFTStakerDepletion, NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady) with no shared base. F-20-03 is the first materialised instance of the hazard, and it materialised IN THE SAME COMMIT that added the copy — and in the reverse direction the watch note anticipated: the fix landed in the new clone and was never back-ported to the original.
findings.deviation: RECURRENCE, not a new class. This is `WATCH-17-maintenance-coupling-drift` (opened run-17 for the PriceScaled clone, widened run-18 to cover two clones). It should be widened again to THREE clones and, per F-20-03, promoted from a watch note to an active hazard with a demonstrated instance. Under Law 3 this is a non-obvious owner/maintainer footgun (a competent maintainer fixing NFTStakerDepletion would reasonably not expect the fix to already exist elsewhere), so it stays in scope as an operational hazard rather than being suppressed as a design preference.
findings.recommendation: Do not re-litigate the no-shared-base design decision (Law 3 trusts it). Do (a) widen WATCH-17 to all three clones, (b) add a mandatory next-run step diffing all four stakers pairwise, and (c) land F-20-03 as the concrete back-port.

findings.specText: docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.1: "**It is now an untrusted-input check on a value an attacker fully controls, and it is the thing standing between a caller and the payment-token balance held mid-transaction.** Two distinct failures it prevents: claiming the contract's payment-token balance (accumulated sub-threshold dust from prior batches) as 'reward'; ..." and §6 test 4: "`test_PaymentTokenDustNotClaimableAsReward`."
findings.actualBehavior: The §4.1 guard is correctly and unconditionally implemented (src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:426-428), but its stated threat model overstates what it protects. Step 10's dust sweep (line 381-384) already transfers the contract's ENTIRE payment-token balance to `msg.sender` whenever it is >= DUST_THRESHOLD (1e6 wei — i.e. 1e-12 of an 18dp USDS), on a `count == 1` call with empty reward arrays, with no `nudgeSize` qualification required. Empirically proven (workspace PoC, PASS): a 500-USDS balance donated to the contract is swept in full to a non-qualifying caller, and `batchMint` returns `totalPaid == 0` while the caller is net positive. §4.1's narrow claim about SUB-threshold dust does hold (`remaining / DUST_THRESHOLD == 0` leaves it in place); the broader framing ("the thing standing between a caller and the payment-token balance") does not.
findings.deviation: Spec-prose overstatement, not a code deviation. The sweep behaviour is pre-existing, contract-documented ("A griefer who pre-deposits payment-token to this contract simply donates to the next caller", src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:68) and explicitly preserved by §4.6, so the implementation is faithful; the normative doc's justification is what is wrong. The `totalPaid` floor-at-zero on a net-positive call is likewise pre-existing and §4.6-preserved, but it means the return value silently mis-reports the caller's true net spend.
findings.recommendation: Correct §4.1's wording to scope the claim to sub-threshold dust and to the snapshot/refund-accounting perturbation. No code change required.

findings.specText: commit 2bf13cb body: "drops ... the meaningless USDC != TOKEN_MINTER require"; script/DeployBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:41-46: "The old 'nudge token == payment token' deploy guard is gone: that collision is now checked ON-CHAIN, per call, against every element of the caller's `rewardTokens` array (`BatchMint__RewardTokenIsPaymentToken`)."
findings.actualBehavior: The on-chain per-call check is NOT an equivalent replacement for the removed deploy-time assertion — it reverts the CALLER, it does not warn the OPERATOR. If `DISPATCHER_INDEX` is pointed at a dispatcher whose `primeToken()` equals the token the same dispatcher donates to `batchMinter`, the nudge is structurally dead: every attempt to claim it reverts `BatchMint__RewardTokenIsPaymentToken`, and the accumulated pot is instead swept to whichever caller next runs a 1-mint batch (F-20-05). This is not hypothetical — `yield-claim-nft/src/dispatchers/PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol` has `primeToken() == USDC` (line 189-191) AND donates USDC to `batchMinter` (line 340), and `NudgeRatchet.sol` likewise forwards USDC to `batchMinter` under a 6-decimal deploy guard. Only the currently-pinned `BalancerPoolerV2` (index 4, `primeToken` = USDS, donates USDC) is safe. The script's own NatSpec flags `DISPATCHER_INDEX = 4` as "ASSUMED ... the operator MUST confirm", so a repoint is an expected operation.
findings.deviation: The removal of the deploy guard is faithful to the commit message, but the stated equivalence ("checked ON-CHAIN, per call") does not hold for the operator-facing failure mode the old guard existed to catch. Non-obvious owner footgun under Law 3: a competent, non-malicious operator repointing DISPATCHER_INDEX would be surprised that the nudge silently becomes unclaimable and leaks.
findings.recommendation: Restore an operator-facing guard in the deploy script (and/or a `setDispatcherIndex` sanity log): resolve `configs(DISPATCHER_INDEX).dispatcher.primeToken()` and assert it differs from the intended reward asset for that dispatcher. Cheap, deploy-time only, and it restores the operator signal the on-chain check cannot give.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "NFTStakerPriceScaled verbatim plus the story-019 owner-driven migration block"
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: `diff -u src/NFTStakerPriceScaled.sol src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol` yields no undeclared behavioural delta. Every hunk maps onto one of the six deltas enumerated in the new contract's own NatSpec (lines 21-67). The only extra is header prose (a dropped reference to the product-owner `variable-runway.md` path). `priceScale` immutable, its zero-guard (line 317) and the single `latestPrice = latestPrice * priceScale` multiply (line 582) are carried over intact.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "NFTStaker.sol, NFTStakerPriceScaled.sol, NFTStakerDepletion.sol, both migrators, INFTStakerMigratable and all existing tests are untouched"
conformingClaimsVerified.verdict: CONFORMING (literally true, but see F-20-03 — being literally true is the defect)
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: `git show --stat f65aec9` lists exactly three files, all additions: src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol (+1005), test/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.t.sol (+717), test/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigratorOrchestrators.t.sol (+399).

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "`depositFor` carries a tail `_recomputeSchedule()` — load-bearing, not cosmetic"
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: Present at src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:901. It is load-bearing because R = S * targetAPY / SECONDS_PER_YEAR with S = totalStaked * latestPrice (CLAUDE.md invariant 3). `depositFor`'s head `_syncBudget()` (line 882) recomputes at the PRE-mutation `totalStaked`; without the tail, R stays sized for the smaller pre-deposit pool. Failure mode without it: every staker under-earns relative to `targetAPY` until the next stake/unstake/pullAndRefresh — i.e. an APY-target (Law-2) breach, not a solvency breach; the direction is conservative, so no over-emission. This is exactly why the equivalent tail in `NFTStakerDepletion` is only cosmetic (its rate is budget/window, totalStaked-independent).

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "`depositFor` settles existing pending via `_safePayTo(user, ...)` rather than `_safePay(...)`, which would pay the migrator"
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:888 uses `_safePayTo(user, pending)`; `_exitPosition` (line 856) likewise uses `_safePayTo(account, pending)`. `_safePayTo` (line 706) transfers to the explicit `account`, and `_safePay` (line 692) preserves the msg.sender form for stake/unstake/claim. The guard genuinely prevents migrator capture. (The same claim is FALSE for the pre-existing NFTStakerDepletion — see F-20-03.)

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "the frozen snapshot cannot move while Migrating"
conformingClaimsVerified.verdict: CONFORMING on the accrual path (which is the scope the story claims); NOT total, and the code says so
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: Complete enumeration: rewardRate/rewardBudget/windowEnd are written ONLY in `_recomputeSchedule` (lines 606-608). Its callers are: `_syncBudget` (2 sites, both routed through `_recomputeScheduleIfActive`, lines 463/469), the `stake` tail (642) and `unstake` tail (663) — both routed; `depositFor` tail (901) — unrouted but `require(poolState == Active)` at line 881; `finalizeAndReset` (930) — deliberate, flips to Active first; and the four owner setters `setDispatcherIndex` (375), `setNFTMinter` (386), `setTargetAPY` (399), `topUp` (412), plus `rescueERC20` (439) — all unrouted and callable while Migrating. So the property is total on the user-interaction path and deliberately non-total on the owner path, exactly as documented at lines 476-481. Assessed as BENIGN: `_updatePool` fully no-ops while Migrating (line 498), so a moved rate/window cannot accrue anything, and `finalizeAndReset` re-derives the whole schedule against the drained pool before Active resumes. `rewardBudget` recomputation during Migrating stays consistent because `_safePayTo` decrements it symmetrically on each exit. NOTE: the commit-message phrasing is an absolute; the NatSpec is honest. Only the commit message overstates.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "finalizeAndReset re-derives the schedule against the drained pool, matching unstake-to-zero (rate 0, windowEnd == now)"
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: Line 926-931: requires Migrating, requires totalStaked == 0, fast-forwards lastRewardTime, flips to Active BEFORE calling `_recomputeSchedule()` so the recompute is not swallowed by the Migrating guard. At totalStaked == 0, S == 0 -> rate 0 and windowEnd == block.timestamp, byte-identical to an unstake-to-zero.
`diff` of the two `rescueERC20` bodies is empty — byte-identical, including the rewardToken branch (`_updatePool` -> transfer -> `balanceOf >= committedDebt` assert -> `_recomputeSchedule`).

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "the two new test suites prove both orchestrators work against the new staker with no source changes, including a cross-model Depletion -> PriceScaled migration"
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: test/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.t.sol (717 lines) + test/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigratorOrchestrators.t.sol (399 lines) added; INFTStakerMigratable and both migrators unchanged; `forge test` at HEAD: 333 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
None of the four identifiers appear anywhere in src/ or script/ at HEAD.
src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:119, :121, :133 — signatures match §2 of the spec exactly, including the 3-field `(address token, uint256 minReward, uint256 actualReward)`.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "inherit OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard (non-transient, matching NFTStaker.sol) and apply nonReentrant to batchMint"
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: Import of `@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol` (line 11, non-transient variant as required by the solc 0.8.20 pin), inherited at line 82, `nonReentrant` on `batchMint` at line 300. Note (strengthening beyond spec): `_snapshotRewards` is declared `private view`, so the caller-supplied `balanceOf` calls compile to STATICCALL and cannot reenter at all; the only caller-controlled hook is the payout-pass `transfer`, which `nonReentrant` covers.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "batchMint(count, recipient, paymentAmount, rewardTokens[], minRewards[]) implementing normative steps 1-10 in order"
conformingClaimsVerified.verdict: CONFORMING — order verified step by step against §3
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: 1 validate count/recipient/length (302-306); 2 resolve minter/index/dispatcher/primeToken (310-323); 3 qualifies = nudgeSize != 0 && count >= nudgeSize (349-353); 4 pre-loop snapshot pass (354 -> 416-436); 5 safeTransferFrom pull (357); 6 forceApprove max (360); 7 mint loop (363-365); 8 forceApprove 0 (368); 9 payout pass (378 -> 452-461); 10 dust sweep + totalPaid (381-387). No reordering. Security-relevant consequence verified: step 8 revokes the max approval BEFORE step 9 hands control to caller-supplied token code, so a malicious reward token can never reach an outstanding payment-token allowance.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "4.1 payment-token exclusion runs unconditionally on every element inside the snapshot pass, before any funds move"
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:426-428 — the equality check precedes the `qualifies ? balanceOf : 0` ternary on line 429 and is inside the per-element loop, and the whole pass runs at line 354, ahead of the line-357 pull. A non-qualifying caller therefore cannot probe payment-token balances via the reward path. (See F-20-05 for the separate, pre-existing sweep path, and F-20-06 for the operator-facing gap.)

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "4.2 snapshot taken BEFORE the mint loop, with the do-not-simplify warning at BOTH the snapshot site and the payout site"
conformingClaimsVerified.verdict: CONFORMING for the single-entry case; DEFEATED by duplicates (F-20-01)
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: Snapshot at line 354 precedes the loop at 363; payout at 378 follows it. The DO-NOT-SIMPLIFY warning appears at the call site (327-344), on `_snapshotRewards` (392-399) and on `_payRewards` (440-447) — three sites, exceeding the two the commit claims. `test_OwnDonationsDoNotRefundToBatcher` exists with §4.2-naming failure messages, as §4.2 requires.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: "NatSpec: 4.4 fee-on-transfer paragraph, 4.5 own-risk one-liner, contract-level claimable-by-anyone warning, and a re-framed rescueERC20 docstring"
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: §4.4 paragraph at lines 252-256 (wording matches the spec's mandated caller's-terms text); §4.5 one-liner at 258-266; contract-level WARNING at 51-61 including the honeypot rebuttal and the 'error was in the sender' sentence; rescueERC20 re-framed at 190-207 as 'a race the owner will usually lose' with the 'pause first, then rescue' prescription.

conformingClaimsVerified.verdict: CONFORMING on names and count; one witness is vacuous (F-20-02)
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: All 21 §6 test names present verbatim in test/BatchNFTMinterMultiTokenNudge.t.sol, including the reentrancy witness, the fee-on-transfer witness (which correctly asserts delivered < declared floor, encoding §4.4), and the fuzz totalPaid accounting test.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: deploy script drops setNudgePaymentToken, the nudgePaymentToken() post-condition, the USDC constant/log, and the 'meaningless' USDC != TOKEN_MINTER require, while keeping the SYA.setNudgeAddress 30% drip context
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: git show 2bf13cb -- script/DeployBatchNFTMinter.s.sol: all four removals present; the `SYA.setNudgeAddress(<this>) (PRIMARY 30% drip)` operator step is retained and annotated 'UNCHANGED by the multi-token nudge'; remaining guards (unset minter / unset dispatcher index / zero nudge size / unset pauser) and post-conditions match the revised NatSpec. See F-20-06 for the residual operator-signal gap the removal opens.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: §4.4 fee-on-transfer — who bears the loss (Law-1 override question 3)
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: The loss falls entirely on the caller/recipient, who chose the token: `minRewards[i]` is checked against the contract's pre-transfer snapshot (line 431) and the contract transfers `snapshot[i]`, so the contract's own accounting is exact and no other user is affected. `minRewards` can indeed be satisfied while the recipient nets less — this is stated in the NatSpec in the caller's own terms and pinned by `test_FeeOnTransferDeliversBelowMinReward`. Deliberate, self-harming-only, correctly disclosed.

conformingClaimsVerified.claim: caller-chosen arbitrary token list — worst case (Law-1 override question 1)
conformingClaimsVerified.verdict: SAFE AS SPECIFIED apart from F-20-01 — no additional finding
conformingClaimsVerified.evidence: The contract holds no ERC1155 (mints route straight to `recipient`), holds no user deposits, and carries no outstanding approval at payout time (revoked at line 368 before line 378). A malicious reward token's `balanceOf` is STATICCALL-reached; its `transfer` is behind `nonReentrant`, and every other state-changing entry point is `onlyOwner` or `onlyPauser`. A reverting or non-ERC20 address only reverts the caller's own batch. The residual exposure is exactly what §1 intends: any non-payment-token balance is claimable by a qualifying caller, and qualifying costs more in real mints than the pot is worth.

ledgerReconciliation.label: L-01
ledgerReconciliation.title: batchMint lacks nonReentrant; ERC1155 onERC1155Received fires mid-loop
ledgerReconciliation.basis: story-022 §4.3 adds OZ ReentrancyGuard + `nonReentrant` on `batchMint` (src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:82, :300). The caller-chosen `recipient` still receives ERC1155 mid-loop, but the callback can no longer reenter `batchMint`. Human application only.

ledgerReconciliation.label: L-02
ledgerReconciliation.title: Uncapped count loop in batchMint
ledgerReconciliation.basis: docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.5: "**Long arrays**: gas is paid by the caller; the block gas limit is the bound." The same rationale is applied to `count`.

ledgerReconciliation.label: L-03
ledgerReconciliation.title: Nudge-token equality guard reverts even when nudge is size-disabled
ledgerReconciliation.proposal: CLOSE as moot / DO-NOT-FIX — premise inverted by story-022
ledgerReconciliation.basis: The remedy L-03 implies (skip the equality guard when the nudge is disabled/non-qualifying) is now DIRECTLY CONTRARY to spec. docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.1 and §3 step 4 require the check to run "*unconditionally, even when `qualifies` is false*, so a non-qualifying call can never probe payment-token balances", pinned by `test_RevertWhen_RewardTokenIsPaymentToken_EvenWhenNotQualifying`. Applying L-03 would reintroduce a probe vector. Flagging loudly so triage does not 'fix' it.

ledgerReconciliation.label: L-04
ledgerReconciliation.title: hardcodes assumed DISPATCHER_INDEX / USDC nudge token with no on-chain verification
ledgerReconciliation.basis: The hardcoded USDC nudge-token half is gone (constant, setter call, post-condition and log all removed by 2bf13cb). The hardcoded `DISPATCHER_INDEX = 4` half remains, still with only a prose 'operator MUST confirm'. F-20-06 raises the stakes on that half.

ledgerReconciliation.label: L-05
ledgerReconciliation.title: minReward==0 default silently opts out of the slippage guard
ledgerReconciliation.proposal: no change — premise intact, marginally widened
ledgerReconciliation.basis: `0` remains 'no floor' (src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:287, spec §2). New adjacent case: an empty `rewardTokens` array means no floor at all, but it also means no reward is wanted, so the opt-out is explicit rather than silent. The wont-fix rationale still holds.

ledgerReconciliation.label: L-08 / L-02 / L-03 (NFTStakerDepletion migration-block Lows) / M-02 (NFTStaker)
ledgerReconciliation.title: inherited-by-clone open findings
ledgerReconciliation.proposal: record as inherited on the new file; do NOT mint new fingerprints
ledgerReconciliation.basis: The new clone carries verbatim: L-08 (unchecked `priceScale` magnitude, line 317 guards only zero), NFTStakerDepletion L-02 (un-try/catch'd `dispatcherHook.pull()` in `_syncBudget`), NFTStakerDepletion L-03 (stake/unstake/claim not poolState-gated during `Migrating` — no auto-pause), and NFTStaker M-02 (wont-fix, `emergencyWithdraw` skips recompute). Precedent for the M-02 case exists in the ledger as the [SUPPRESSED-CONTEXT] entry on the PriceScaled copy; apply the same treatment. NFTStakerDepletion's other two Lows (unconditional tail window-restart, finalizeAndReset not re-arming the depletion window) are depletion-model-specific and do NOT transfer.

notes: Scan was read-only against lib/phoenix-nft-staking; `git status --porcelain` clean after `forge test`.
Empirical work was done in workspace/phoenix-nft-staking at 0d1a0b2 (writable clone), never in lib/.

Production-config grounding for F-20-01/F-20-06 came from lib/yield-claim-nft dispatchers: BalancerPoolerV2 (pinned index 4) has primeToken = USDS and donates USDC to `batchMinter`; PromotionUniV2_Eth has primeToken == USDC AND donates USDC; NudgeRatchet forwards USDC to `batchMinter`.
